HasUponPickupEffect.maps_to: no counterpart -- byrdpip.py does not set has_upon_pickup_effect
HasUponPickupEffect.issue: Byrdpip.cs:24 declares `HasUponPickupEffect => true` and the sim's Relic base has the exact field for it (relics/base.py:96), which fourteen other ports set. Byrdpip leaves it at the False default. DORMANT (executed -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py batch3`): the flag's only sim consumer is Relic.is_tradable (relics/base.py:132), and EVENT rarity already excludes the relic there, so the probe reports `has_upon_pickup_effect=False spawns_pets=False adds_pet=True is_tradable=False` -- the right answer by the wrong route. SpawnsPets.maps_to: no counterpart -- byrdpip.py does not set spawns_pets
SpawnsPets.issue: Byrdpip.cs:26 declares `SpawnsPets => true`; relics/base.py:132 has the field and the port leaves it False. DORMANT, enumerated: `git grep -n spawns_pets sts2_rl/*.py sts2_rl/**/*.py` (excluding .pyc) returns exactly two non-declaration hits in the whole sim -- relics/base.py:132 (the field default) and relics/base.py:166, `Relic.is_tradable`'s `if self.is_used_up or self.has_upon_pickup_effect or self.spawns_pets: return False`. That is the flag's ONLY reader, enumerated exhaustively rather than sampled. And that one reader is already shadowed for this relic: byrdpip.py:20 sets `rarity = RelicRarity.EVENT`, and `is_tradable`'s own second branch excludes EVENT unconditionally (`self.rarity not in (STARTER, EVENT, ANCIENT)`), so the answer is False whether or not spawns_pets is set. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes.py batch3`): `sim has_upon_pickup_effect=False spawns_pets=False adds_pet=True is_tradable=False` -- the right answer by the wrong route. Same dormancy and same executed evidence as HasUponPickupEffect (relic/byrdpip.json's own sibling hook, not owned by this batch). Goes live the moment either (a) anything besides is_tradable reads spawns_pets, or (b) a future EVENT-rarity relic with SpawnsPets/HasUponPickupEffect also loses its EVENT rarity in the port (the two flags would then be load-bearing on their own).

AfterObtained.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and G3 per binding rule 4. The deck half of the Byrdonis Egg -> Byrd Swoop transform is faithful; the combat-pile half (G1) and the mid-combat SummonPet call (G3) are dropped. DORMANT overall -- both halves settle to unreachable on today's content, for two independent reasons. G1 (combat-pile transform): enumerated by listing every RunState.add_relic call site (`git grep -n 'add_relic(' sts2_rl/*.py sts2_rl/**/*.py`, ~30 hits) -- every one of them is inside an event, rest site, shop or treasure-room handler (events/*.py, shop.py, run.py's own map/treasure paths); zero call sites are reached from inside a CombatState. The sim also has no in-combat relic-grant command at all: CombatState never calls RunState.add_relic, so a Byrdonis Egg cannot be sitting in a fight's hand/discard/exhaust pile at the moment this relic is granted, because the grant itself can only happen between fights. G3 (SummonPet): see guard G3's own four-reading enumeration below -- the pet is inert under every ported reader because the sim's CombatState has exactly two participant categories, `self.player` (combat.py:144) and `self.enemies`, with no pet slot to add a creature to in the first place. Porting any mid-combat relic acquisition (G1) or a player-side pet/summon creature (G3) makes this live.

BeforeCombatStart.issue: Byrdpip.cs:64-67 summons the pet at the start of EVERY combat. The port has no on_combat_start. Carries guard G3's verdict; see G3 for why the omission is observationally inert today. DORMANT, enumerated independently of G3's own four readings: the sim's CombatState constructor (combat.py:144) builds exactly `self.player` (a PlayerCombatState) plus an enemy list -- `git grep -n 'pet' sts2_rl/combat.py` returns zero hits, and `git grep -rn 'def summon_pet\|SummonPet' sts2_rl --include=*.py` returns zero hits anywhere in the sim. There is structurally no third participant category for a summoned pet to occupy, so no hook this port could add would have anything to dispatch to. This is a stronger version of G3's per-listener enumeration (which checked the 23 ported implementers of BeforeSideTurnStart/AfterTurnStart/AfterBlockCleared and found each one owner-filtered): even an unfiltered listener could not see the pet, because the pet is never constructed. Goes live only alongside G3 -- the moment any player-side pet/summon creature is modelled in combat, both this hook and G3 need porting together.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): the transform covers the deck only, not the combat piles
guards.issue: Byrdpip.cs:49-53 collects every ByrdonisEgg from the Deck pile and, `if (CombatManager.Instance.IsInProgress)`, ALSO from `Owner.PlayerCombatState.AllCards` -- i.e. a Byrdonis Egg sitting in the draw/hand/discard/exhaust pile of a fight in progress is transformed too. byrdpip.py:25 iterates `run.deck` only. DORMANT for the same reason relic/belt_buckle's AfterObtained is: the sim grants relics through RunState.add_relic between rooms and has no path that obtains a relic inside a combat, and Byrdpip's own grant path is the Byrdonis Egg card's HATCH rest-site option -- a rest site, never a fight. Recorded as a gap rather than a waiver because 'no ported content reaches this' is today's content, not the divergence's shape (binding rule 1). Porting any mid-combat relic grant makes it live.

guards.what: G3: the pet creature (SummonPet, Byrdpip.cs:69-72, from both AfterObtained and BeforeCombatStart) is not modelled at all
guards.rationale: The port's docstring asserts the pet is pure flavour; the claim is checked here rather than trusted (PROMPT.md bug class 12). It holds, on four independent readings. (a) src/Core/Models/Monsters/Byrdpip.cs:12-16 gives it MinInitialHp == MaxInitialHp == 9999 and IsHealthBarVisible false; (b) its GenerateMoveStateMachine (:26-31) is a single MoveState 'NOTHING_MOVE' whose body is `Task.CompletedTask` and whose FollowUpState is itself -- no RNG, no effect; (c) it is never targeted, because monster moves aim at CombatState.PlayerCreatures, which filters `c.IsPlayer` (CombatState.cs:75) and a pet creature is not a player, and it is not in `_enemies` so it never takes a turn; (d) the only content that looks the pet up is ByrdSwoop.cs:28, `WithAttackerAnim(..., GetPet<Byrdpip>())` -- the attack animation origin. PlayerCmd.AddPet<T> (PlayerCmd.cs:237-257) draws no RNG either. WHAT WOULD MAKE IT OBSERVABLE: the pet IS in CombatState.Creatures and therefore in CreaturesOnCurrentSide, so it is a participant for BeforeSideTurnStart / AfterTurnStart / AfterBlockCleared. Every ported listener on those hooks filters on `creature == Owner.Creature` or `participants.Contains(...)` (this batch's relic/captains_wheel, relic/candelabra, relic/chandelier and relic/cloak_clasp all do), so no ported effect can see the extra creature -- porting one that reacts to ANY player-side creature without an owner check would. Verdicted deliberate-divergence rather than gap because the observable outcome is identical under every ported reader (binding rule 2). Rule 7: src/Core/Models/Monsters/Byrdpip.cs, ByrdSwoop.cs, CombatState.cs and PlayerCmd.cs are NOT hashed here.

guards.what: G2: `Skin = new Rng(base.Owner, base.Id).NextItem(SkinOptions)` (Byrdpip.cs:48) and the [SavedProperty] Skin field
guards.rationale: A cosmetic sprite-skin choice with no gameplay reading (its only consumer is src/Core/Models/Monsters/Byrdpip.cs:18-24 SetupSkins). It is also not an RNG-parity concern, which is why it is checked rather than skipped: `new Rng(owner, id)` CONSTRUCTS a fresh independent generator seeded from the owner and the relic id, so it consumes nothing from any RunRngSet stream. Presentation-only under the shared contract.

PROMPT.md bug class 16's second half (a named RNG stream silently falling back to the shared legacy rng) does NOT apply: TransformTo supplies an explicit replacement, and CardTransformation.GetReplacement returns `Replacement` without touching the Rng when it is set (CardTransformation.cs:55-59). The sim's transform_card only rolls when `into is None` (run.py:437), so both sides consume zero draws. Placement also matches: a Deck-pile transform in C# removes the original and APPENDS the replacement at the end (CardCmd.cs:427-437), which run.transform_card's docstring cites and implements. Rule 7: CardCmd.cs, CardTransformation.cs and run.py are not hashed here.
